answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each validator to an identity anchor rooted in a trust graph. When committees evaluate peer transactions, game-theoretic multi-agent auditing enforces topological cut verifications across the cluster. If a colluding cluster attempts an attack beyond the dispute horizon, automated stake slashing destroys their pooled capital. Like resilient juniper roots interlocking soil, superlinear attacker cost scales with graph expansion.
